analysis: The PR touches only the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift. It adds a StubTokenizer.decodeTable (head lines ~146-155), a stopStringScope parameter on the makeBridge helper (~443, ~462), and three new tests (~847-899). The tests cover stop-string scoping: matchedStopSequence with a ReasoningStopScope, per-request scope reaching the engine and the usage signal, and a request scope replacing the model scope. No production code is visible in these units, so there is no new attack surface, no change to authorization, attestation, encryption, cache scoping (T-041), or the billing/usage paths, and no secrets are introduced. The tests assert behavior in which stop strings are not matched inside reasoning spans. That is a correctness property, not a security boundary in the threat model. Unverified: the production changes that implement ReasoningStopScope, submitTokenized(stopStringScope:), and EngineV2Bridge's stopStringScope init parameter are in other files and were not supplied. Whether those changes affect any security conclusion (e.g. stop-string handling affecting usage accounting or output exposure) cannot be judged from this test-only diff. The patch excerpt was truncated, but the base and head ranges are complete per the file_changes map. No findings.
